# Disagreement Log — Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 9

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Chapter:** POX 9 — Joseph chosen by divine sign; his reluctance; Mary enters his house

---

## Disagreements

**1. 9:1 — "adze" vs. "carpenter's axe" vs. "carpenter's tools"**
- EMET: "throwing down his adze"
- LOGOS: "set down his carpenter's axe"
- PNEUMA: "put down his carpenter's tools"
- Note: Greek *tektōn* = carpenter/craftsman. The specific tool word varies by MS. "Adze" is the traditional English translation of the instrument. LOGOS changes to "axe"; PNEUMA generalizes to "tools."

**2. 9:1 — "there was no sign among them"**
- EMET/LOGOS: "no sign among them" / "no sign appeared among them"
- PNEUMA: adds narrative embellishment: "just a roomful of men holding plain wooden sticks"
- Note: PNEUMA's addition has no basis in the Greek text.

**3. 9:2 — "came out from the staff"**
- EMET: "a dove came out from the staff"
- LOGOS: "a dove flew out from his staff"
- PNEUMA: "a dove burst out of it"
- Note: Greek *exēlthen peristera ek tou rabdou* = "a dove came out from the staff." PNEUMA's "burst" adds dramatic force not in the text.

**4. 9:2 — "chosen by lot"**
- EMET: "you have been chosen by lot to receive"
- LOGOS: "You have been chosen to take"
- PNEUMA: "God has chosen you to take"
- Note: EMET inserts "by lot" which is an interpretive addition — the Greek *su pareilēphas* = "you have received/been designated." LOGOS/PNEUMA are closer to the Greek here.

**5. 9:3 — "I shall not be made a laughingstock"**
- EMET: "I shall not be made a laughingstock"
- LOGOS: "I will become a laughingstock"
- PNEUMA: "The people will laugh at me"
- Note: Greek *katagelaston me poiēseis* = "you will make me a laughingstock." EMET/LOGOS preserve the noun; PNEUMA weakens it.

**6. 9:4 — "how the earth was split open and swallowed them up"**
- EMET: "the earth was split open and swallowed them up"
- LOGOS: "the ground split open and swallowed them alive"
- PNEUMA: "the earth opened up and swallowed them whole"
- Note: LOGOS adds "alive" which is not in the text but is from the Numbers narrative. PNEUMA adds "whole." Minor variations; EMET is most literal.

**7. 9:5 — Order of Joseph's farewell**
- EMET: leaves order intact — "I am leaving you... going to build... the Lord will watch... I will return"
- LOGOS: rearranges to: "leaving you... go to work... The Lord will guard... I will return"
- PNEUMA: "I'm leaving you here... go to work... I'll be back. The Lord will look after you" — moves the promise of return before the divine protection
- Note: The Greek word order in EMET is most faithfully preserved.
